In 1970 she became the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.

Teresa de Ahumada entered the Carmelite convent of the Incarnation at Ávila in 1535. For nearly twenty years her prayer was half-hearted, until in 1554 she was overcome before an image of the wounded Christ. From then on she lived a life of deep prayer and mystical graces. In 1562 she founded the small convent of Saint Joseph, returning to the strict original rule, and with Saint John of the Cross she carried the reform to the friars. She travelled Spain in a covered cart, founding convents in spite of illness and opposition, and wrote with humour and honesty about the soul's journey to God. She died at Alba de Tormes in 1582 and was canonised in 1622.
Saint Teresa of Ávila · Prayer to

Saint Teresa, you learned that God alone suffices. Teach me to pray as a friend speaks with a friend, to persevere when prayer is dry, and to keep a good humour on the way. Pray for me, that nothing may disturb me and nothing frighten me. Amen.
Let nothing disturb you, let nothing frighten you. All things are passing; God never changes. Patience obtains all things. Whoever has God lacks nothing. God alone suffices.
Prayer, Teresa said, is nothing else than an intimate sharing between friends. Speak to Christ today as a friend.

A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial to whom Christ revealed His Sacred Heart in a series of visions between 1673 and 1675. Doubted by her community, she persevered, and the devotion to the Sacred Heart spread through the whole Church, with its First Fridays and the feast of the Sacred Heart.

Margaret Mary entered the Visitation monastery at Paray-le-Monial in 1671. In a series of revelations Christ showed her His Heart, burning with love and wounded by ingratitude, and asked for a feast in its honour, for Communion on the first Friday of each month, and for an hour of prayer on Thursday nights in memory of His agony in Gethsemane. Her community thought her deluded until the Jesuit Saint Claude de la Colombière recognised the visions as genuine. The devotion she spread became one of the most widely loved in the Church. She was canonised in 1920.
Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque · Prayer to

Saint Margaret Mary, you saw the Heart that has so loved the world. Pray that my cold heart may be warmed by it, that I may make reparation for my sins and the sins of the world, and that I may rest in that Heart at the hour of my death. Amen.
Behold this Heart which has so loved men. Make an act of reparation today for indifference to that love.

Bishop of Antioch, taken under guard to Rome to be thrown to the beasts. On the way he wrote seven letters to the churches, the earliest witness outside Scripture to bishops, the Eucharist and the name 'Catholic Church'.

Ignatius was the third bishop of Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians. Arrested under Trajan around 107, he was taken in chains across Asia Minor to Rome. On the way he wrote seven letters, to the Ephesians, Magnesians, Trallians, Romans, Philadelphians and Smyrnaeans, and to Bishop Polycarp. They are the earliest writings we have that speak of bishops, priests and deacons, of the Eucharist as the flesh of Christ, and of 'the Catholic Church'. He begged the Christians of Rome not to try to save him. He died in the arena.
Saint Ignatius of Antioch · Prayer to

Saint Ignatius, you went to your death longing to be wheat ground into the bread of Christ. Pray that I may love the Eucharist as you did, stay close to the Church, and not shrink from what following Christ will cost. Amen.
I am the wheat of God, and I am ground by the teeth of wild beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of Christ. What in you does God wish to grind into bread?

A Greek physician and companion of Saint Paul who wrote the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. Only Luke gives us the Annunciation, the Visitation, the Magnificat, the Benedictus, the shepherds, the Prodigal Son and the Good Samaritan. Tradition says he painted the first icon of the Virgin.

Saint Paul calls him 'Luke, the most dear physician'. A Gentile, probably from Antioch, Luke travelled with Paul, and the 'we' passages of Acts are his eyewitness account. He wrote his Gospel 'in order', having carefully traced everything from the beginning, and his pages carry the infancy of Christ, the parables of mercy and the canticles the Church still prays every day. He is the patron of physicians, surgeons and artists.
Saint Luke the Evangelist · Prayer to

Saint Luke, physician and evangelist, you wrote of the mercy of God for the poor and the lost. Pray for all who care for the sick, for doctors and nurses, and for me, that I may know myself found by the Shepherd who came to seek the lost. Amen.

O Lord, we beseech You, that Luke, Your holy Evangelist, who for the honor of Your name bore continually in his body the suffering of the cross, may intercede in our behalf. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Read Luke 15 slowly today, the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son.

Karol Wojtyła, actor, philosopher and bishop of Kraków, was elected pope in 1978, the first non-Italian in 455 years. He helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe, travelled to 129 countries, gave the Church the Theology of the Body and the Catechism, and bore his long final illness in public.

Born in Wadowice in 1920, Karol Wojtyła lost his mother, brother and father by the age of twenty. Under Nazi occupation he worked in a quarry, acted in an underground theatre and studied secretly for the priesthood. As bishop and archbishop of Kraków he defended the Church against the communist regime. Elected pope in 1978, he travelled the world, began World Youth Day, survived an assassin's bullet in 1981 and visited the gunman in prison to forgive him. He established Divine Mercy Sunday, gave the Church the Catechism, and died on its vigil in 2005. He was canonised in 2014.
Saint John Paul II · Prayer to

Saint John Paul, you told the world not to be afraid. Pray for me in my fears, for families and young people, and for the Church you loved. Help me to open wide the doors of my life to Christ, and to trust in His mercy. Amen.
Do not be afraid. Open wide the doors for Christ. Which door have you kept shut?

Two of the Twelve, kept together because tradition holds that they preached in Persia and were martyred there together. Simon is called the Zealot; Jude, also named Thaddeus, wrote the short letter that bears his name and is the patron of hopeless causes.

Simon is called the Zealot, perhaps because he had belonged to the party that resisted Rome, perhaps for his zeal. Jude, also called Thaddeus, is the apostle who asked Christ at the Last Supper why He would show Himself to them and not to the world. He wrote the short Letter of Jude, urging the faithful to 'contend for the faith once delivered to the saints'. Western tradition holds that the two preached together in Persia and were martyred there.
Saints Simon and Jude · Prayer to

Saint Jude, faithful apostle and patron of things despaired of, I bring you what I cannot fix. Pray for me in this need, and teach me to trust in the God for whom nothing is impossible. Saint Simon, pray that my zeal may be for Christ alone. Amen.

O God, Who have given us a way of coming to know Your name through Your blessed Apostles Simon and Jude, grant us to honor their everlasting glory by becoming more holy and to become more holy by honoring it. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Bring to Saint Jude the situation you have given up on.

The Church honours in one feast all who have reached heaven, the great multitude which no man could number, most of them known only to God. The feast was fixed on 1 November in the eighth century and is a holy day of obligation.

The early Church kept the feasts of the martyrs on the anniversaries of their deaths. As their number grew beyond counting, a common feast emerged. In 609 Pope Boniface IV dedicated the Pantheon in Rome to Our Lady and all the martyrs, and in the eighth century Gregory III dedicated a chapel in Saint Peter's to all the saints on 1 November. Gregory IV extended the feast to the whole Church. It honours the saints we know and the vast company we do not, many of them ordinary men and women.

All you holy men and women, saints of God, pray for us. You have finished the race; help us to run it. Win for us the grace to become what God made us to be, and to join you in the vision of His face. Amen.

Almighty, eternal God, Who granted us to honor the merits of all Your Saints in a single solemn festival, bestow on us, we beseech You, through their manifold intercession, that abundance of Your mercy for which we yearn. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Holiness is not for a few. Ask one saint to be your companion this month.

The day after All Saints the Church prays for all who have died in God's friendship but still await purification. Priests may offer three Masses today. Through November Catholics visit graves and pray for their dead.

The custom of praying for the dead is older than Christianity; Judas Maccabeus 'made atonement for the dead, that they might be delivered from their sin'. Saint Odilo, abbot of Cluny, ordered a day of prayer for all the faithful departed around 998, and it spread through the whole Church. In 1915 Benedict XV allowed every priest to offer three Masses today, because of the dead of the First World War.

O Lord, by whose mercy the souls of the faithful find rest, grant to all my family, friends and benefactors who have died the forgiveness of their sins and the light of your face. Holy souls in purgatory, pray for us, and remember us when you come into your kingdom. Amen.
Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace. Amen.
Name your dead before God today, one by one.

Son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed slave, Martin was a Dominican lay brother who served as barber, infirmarian and almoner. He cared for the sick, the poor, slaves and even animals, and was known for his humility and his gift of healing.
He called himself 'the mulatto dog'. Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.

Nephew of Pope Pius IV and cardinal archbishop of Milan, he led the reform of the Church after the Council of Trent, founding seminaries and visiting every parish of his huge diocese. In the plague of 1576 he stayed in the city to nurse the sick when the governor fled.

Safeguard Your Church, O Lord, under the continual protection of St. Charles, Your Confessor and Bishop, so that just as his concern for his flock made him glorious, so his intercession may make us ever fervent in loving You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Reform begins at home. Choose one habit to amend this week.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Life

Saint John Lateran, not Saint Peter's, is the cathedral of the Pope as Bishop of Rome, 'mother and head of all the churches of the city and the world'. It was dedicated by Pope Sylvester in 324, soon after the Church was freed from persecution.
Dedication of the Lateran Basilica · Meditation
You are God's temple. Pray for your own parish church and its priest today.

Pope at a time of collapse, Leo defined the Church's faith that Christ is one Person in two natures, a teaching the Council of Chalcedon received with the cry 'Peter has spoken through Leo'. He met Attila the Hun outside Rome and persuaded him to turn back.
Christian, remember your dignity. What would change if you believed it today?

A Roman soldier who, at the gates of Amiens, cut his cloak in half for a freezing beggar and that night saw Christ wearing it. He became a monk and bishop of Tours, one of the first saints venerated who was not a martyr. His feast fell on the day the 1918 Armistice was signed.

O God, Who see that we cannot survive by any power of our own, mercifully grant that, by the intercession of blessed Martin, Your Confessor and Bishop, we may be made safe from all harm. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Whom will you give half your cloak to this week?
A Dominican friar and bishop who mastered every science of his day, from theology to botany and astronomy, and taught Thomas Aquinas. He is the patron saint of scientists.

O God, Who made blessed Albert, Your Bishop and Doctor, eminent in the submission of human wisdom to divine faith, grant us, we beseech You, so to follow the path of his teaching that we may enjoy perfect light in heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Faith and reason are two wings. Learn one new thing today and thank God for it.

An English princess who married King Malcolm III of Scotland. She reformed the Church in Scotland, founded the abbey at Dunfermline and the Queen's Ferry for pilgrims to Saint Andrews, and fed the poor at her own table before she ate.
Holiness in marriage and family life: do one thing today for those you live with.

A king's daughter and a landgravine who, widowed at twenty, gave her wealth to build a hospital at Marburg and served the sick there herself. She died at twenty-four. Legend says bread she carried to the poor turned to roses when her husband asked to see it.
Give something today that costs you.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Life

An ancient tradition tells that Joachim and Anne brought Mary as a small child to the Temple in Jerusalem to be offered to God. The feast honours her total dedication to God from the beginning of her life.
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Prayer

O God, by Whose will the blessed Mary, ever Virgin, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, was on this day presented in the temple, grant, we beseech You, that by her intercession we may be found worthy to be brought into the temple of Your glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. eiusdem
The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary · Meditation
Offer yourself again to God today, as you are.

A Roman virgin and martyr whose name is said in the Roman Canon. The story of her martyrdom says she sang to God in her heart, and so she became the patron of music and musicians. Her body was found incorrupt in 1599.

O God, Who gladden us by the annual feast of blessed Cecilia, Your Virgin and Martyr, grant, we beseech You, that we may by virtuous conduct follow her whom we venerate in this sacred rite. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Sing, or listen to, one piece of sacred music today with full attention.

A learned young woman of Alexandria who, tradition says, out-argued fifty pagan philosophers sent by the emperor and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered at her touch, she was beheaded. She was one of the voices heard by Saint Joan of Arc.

O God, Who gave the law to Moses on Sinai's height and through your holy angels miraculously placed there the body of blessed Catherine, Your Virgin and Martyr; grant, we beseech You, that by her merits and intercession we may reach that towering eminence which is Christ. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
Love the truth enough to learn it well.

A fisherman of Bethsaida, disciple of John the Baptist, and the first apostle called by Christ. He brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras in Greece, the saltire of Scotland's flag.
We humbly pray Your majesty, O Lord, that, as blessed Andrew was a preacher and ruler in Your Church, so he may always intercede for us with You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Andrew's first act as a disciple was to bring someone else to Jesus. Whom will you bring?

One of the first companions of Saint Ignatius of Loyola, he became the greatest missionary since Saint Paul, preaching in India, the Malay archipelago and Japan, and baptising tens of thousands. He died on an island off the coast of China, waiting to enter it.

O God, You Who were pleased to gather into Your Church the peoples of the Indies by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis, mercifully grant that we, who honor his glorious merits, may also imitate the example of his virtues. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his soul? Ignatius asked him this until he gave his life away.

Bishop of Myra in Asia Minor, remembered for secretly giving three bags of gold to save three poor girls from ruin by throwing them through a window at night. From that hidden charity came Santa Claus.

O God, You who made the holy Bishop Nicholas renowned for countless miracles, grant, we beseech You, that by his merits and prayers we may be saved from the fires of hell. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

A Roman governor acclaimed bishop of Milan by the people while still unbaptised. He wrote hymns still sung in the Divine Office, defended the Church against emperors, and his preaching helped bring Saint Augustine to faith.

O God, who didst give blessed Ambrósii to be thy people’s minister in eternal salvation; grant, we pray, that we who have him for teacher of life here on earth, may also deserve now that he is in heaven, to have him for an advocate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Ambrose made an emperor do public penance. Where do you need to repent publicly, even in a small way?

The Church teaches that Mary, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Christ, was preserved free from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Pius IX defined the dogma in 1854; four years later Our Lady told Bernadette at Lourdes, 'I am the Immaculate Conception.'
O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.
Tota pulchra es, Maria. Ask her to help you hate one particular sin.

In December 1531 the Virgin appeared to Juan Diego, a poor Aztec convert, on the hill of Tepeyac. As a sign for the bishop she filled his cloak with Castilian roses, and when he opened it her image was found printed on it. Millions were baptised in the years that followed.
Am I not here, I who am your mother? Bring her your greatest worry.

A young Christian of Syracuse in Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means light, and her feast, near the darkest days of the year, is kept with candles, especially in Scandinavia. She is named in the Roman Canon.

Graciously hear us, O God of our salvation; that as we rejoice in the festivity of blessed Luciæ Vírginis tuæ, we may be instructed in the affections of a loving devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Be a light in someone's darkness today.
Saint John of the Cross · Life

A Carmelite friar who worked with Saint Teresa of Ávila to reform his order and was imprisoned by his own brothers for it. In a tiny cell in Toledo he wrote his greatest poetry. The Dark Night and The Living Flame of Love map the way of the soul to union with God.
Saint John of the Cross · Meditation
In the evening of life we shall be judged on love.

One of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles to serve the poor, Stephen was stoned to death in Jerusalem for his preaching, praying for his killers as he died. A young man named Saul held the cloaks of those who stoned him.

Grant us, we beseech You, O Lord, to imitate what we celebrate, so that we may learn to love even our enemies; because we keep the anniversary of the invention of Him Who knew how to plead even for His persecutors with our Lord, Jesus Christ, Your Son. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
Lord, do not hold this sin against them. Forgive someone today.

The beloved disciple, who leaned on the Lord's breast at the Last Supper, stood at the foot of the cross and took Mary into his home. He wrote the fourth Gospel, three letters and the Apocalypse, and is the only apostle believed not to have died a martyr.

O Lord, graciously shed light upon Your Church, so that, enlightened by the teachings of blessed John, Your Apostle and Evangelist, she may gain Your everlasting rewards. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Little children, love one another. In old age, they say, this was all he would preach.
The children of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. The Church honours them as martyrs, who confessed Christ not by speaking but by dying.

O God, Whose praise the Innocents, Your martyrs, this day proclaimed, not by speaking, but by dying, put to death in us all the wickedness of sin, so that Your faith which our tongue professes may be proclaimed also by our life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
Pray today for children who suffer, born and unborn.

Chancellor and friend of King Henry II, Thomas became Archbishop of Canterbury and defended the freedom of the Church against the king. Four knights murdered him in his own cathedral. Canterbury became one of the great pilgrim shrines of Europe.
Willing to die for the Church: what would you be willing to give up for her?
